cohort: The study included 1,218,452 childbirths from women with and without congenital heart disease in Norway between 1994 and 2014.
finding: Maternal congenital heart disease (CHD) was associated with higher risks of induced labor and cesarean delivery compared to women without heart disease.
mod_finding: The increase in induced labor was steeper for women with CHD than for those without, while cesarean delivery rates rose in women with mild CHD but remained stable in those with moderate/severe CHD between 1994 and 2014.
